_comment: The debug overlay's switches. Every one is VIEW ONLY: a switch here may hide something or stop something repainting, and may never touch the simulation. That is the property that makes the overlay safe to leave in a build, because a battle plays out identically whatever is switched off (CLAUDE.md 5.2).
_kinds: bool is on or off. cycle steps through values, and the first is the default. nodes are combat screen paths hidden when a bool flag is off; a flag with no nodes only gates work. part names the timing bucket the flag owns, which src/ui/hud_profile.gd accumulates and the panel prints beside the caption, so the list reads worst first without anybody having to toggle anything.
_history: This list used to switch off the 3D scene: starfield, nebulae, deck grid, weapon arcs, impact flares, terrain, world art, plan inset, render scale. They are gone, retired by one reading on the phone the overlay exists for: 45.8 ms a frame, of which 38.4 was script and 7.4 was everything the renderer does. Eighty four percent of the frame was our own GDScript, so which pixels the 3D scene draws was not the question, and nine switches for it were nine ways to ask the wrong one. The list is the interface now, one flag per panel, because that is where the time goes.

hud.label: ALL UI
hud.cost: the whole 2D interface, drawn and updated
hud.note: Every panel below at once, plus the screen space labels. The battle and the 3D view carry on and this overlay stays, so what it removes is the interface and nothing else. Ask this one first: it says how much of the frame is worth chasing before you spend time on which part of it.

ship.label: Ship
ship.note: Hull name, boxes, speed, heading and the ordered throttle.

power.label: Power
power.note: The reactor budget and its five sinks. Each row repaints a strip of discrete boxes as long as the reactor's surviving output.

damage.label: Damage log
damage.cost: 2 autowrapped labels, one line per damaged system
damage.note: The damage report walks every system every tick to build its list, and the comm log rejoins its last six lines.

keep.label: Keep station
keep.cost: 4 tabs and whichever station is open
keep.note: The left tab strip and its panel: repair, life, cargo, lab.

target.label: Target
target.cost: 2 labels and a sensor lock test
target.note: Contact, boxes, range and bearing. The lock test asks the terrain whether the contact can be seen, which is a segment solve per feature.

own_ssd.label: Own ship display
own_ssd.cost: a painted shield ring and 32 subsystem slots
own_ssd.note: The largest single widget in the interface by node count. Its ring paints in _draw and each slot is a texture and two rects.

target_ssd.label: Target display
target_ssd.note: The same component as the own ship display, drawn smaller and read only.

fight.label: Fight station
fight.cost: 6 tabs and whichever station is open
fight.note: The right tab strip and its panel: shields, reactor, sensors, tractor, marines, shuttle.

weapons.label: Weapons
weapons.cost: one row per mount, each running a firing check
weapons.note: Every row asks the ship whether that mount could fire, and each of those runs an arc test, a lock test and a range test against the terrain. It is the most simulation work the interface causes.

overlays.label: Overlays
overlays.cost: brackets, ship labels, sticks and the plan inset
overlays.note: Everything drawn over the battle rather than beside it. The only part that updates every frame rather than at the HUD rate, because the camera moves and the labels have to follow it.

hud_hz.label: UI repaint
hud_hz.cost: how often the panels above are updated
hud_hz.note: Update rate only. It does not reduce what is DRAWN, because Godot has no partial 2D redraw and every visible item is recorded every frame regardless. So this moving very little while the interface is still most of the frame is the expected result rather than a broken switch.
